payload.arrival_context: Sophie found this through a Google search for 'wedding ceremony script australia' while we were weighing up marrying legally in Sydney and celebrating overseas.

first_impression.reaction: Sophie here. I'm a lawyer, so an intro that quotes section 46(1) and section 45(2) straight away is exactly what I wanted, not another US 'by the power vested in me' page. The first sentence is a mouthful though. I had to read it twice, and James would skim straight past it. Then 'Everything else is yours.' landed nicely. It told us the legal bit is small and the rest is ours to write, so we kept going.

journey.quote: In Australia, a celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination must say the monitum in section 46(1) of the Marriage Act 1961, which opens "I am duly authorised by law to solemnise marriages according to law", or words to that effect, before you are married.
journey.reaction: Accurate and sourced, but it's one very long sentence, and it uses the word 'monitum' before explaining what it is. I followed it. James would have given up halfway.
Good. That's the reassurance we wanted. The ceremony can feel like us and not like a template.

journey.section: What the law requires in an Australian wedding ceremony
journey.quote: The celebrant must also meet each of you separately and in person beforehand, and must be physically present to solemnise the marriage, together with the two of you and 2 witnesses.
journey.reaction: This is the kind of detail that trips people up if they're living overseas or travelling for work. It's clear and it links to the source. I trust this.

journey.section: The Australian wedding ceremony script, word for word
journey.quote: This script is written for a civil celebrant. The legal words are set in place; the rest you can keep, cut or rewrite with your celebrant.
journey.reaction: Very usable. With every block marked 'Legally required' or 'Optional' I can hand it to our celebrant and say 'keep these, rewrite these'.

journey.quote: Celebrant: "These rings hold everything you have just said to each other."
journey.reaction: Slightly greeting-card. If our celebrant read that out, a few of our friends would smirk. The rest of the sample wording is restrained, but this line is trying a bit hard.

journey.quote: For a small legal ceremony before a larger celebration, this is the core with nothing added.
journey.reaction: This is our likely plan: sign the papers quietly in Sydney, then do the real celebration somewhere else. Seeing the bare minimum in four steps is really useful.

journey.quote: If this ceremony is one moment in a longer weekend, with guests flying in and a venue to secure, Wedded Concierge plans the whole celebration around it.
journey.reaction: It's fine that you're selling something, but it lands in the middle of a script, and 'plans the whole celebration' is exactly the vague 'end-to-end' line every planner uses. What does it actually cover? The overseas section explains it much better.

journey.section: Witnesses, the signing and the paperwork on the day
journey.quote: Errors on the certificates can be corrected only while the two of you and your witnesses are still present; once the marriage is registered, only the registry's authorised officer can correct them.
journey.reaction: Insider-level detail. Most guides don't tell you this. It's the sort of thing that makes me think the people behind this know what goes wrong on the day.

journey.section: Witnesses, the signing and the paperwork on the day
journey.quote: Choose two people who will stand close by throughout, not anyone with a job to do.
journey.reaction: Practical and honest. My instinct was to pick the best man, who'll be juggling rings and speeches.

journey.section: Marrying overseas or holding a symbolic ceremony
journey.quote: An Australian script does not carry across borders.
journey.reaction: Direct, and saves us from a mistake. Honest trade-off, no fluff.

journey.section: Marrying overseas or holding a symbolic ceremony
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world as your single point of contact from start to finish, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: This is the first time 'end-to-end' gets spelled out. One person, and the fee agreed in writing upfront, speaks directly to my worry about hidden costs. I'd want to know more about who is actually doing the work on the ground.

journey.quote: General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
journey.reaction: I understand why it's there, but I read it six times. By the fourth it was just boilerplate I skipped.

journey.section: Plan the day around the words
journey.quote: When the ceremony is set, your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Quotes in AUD and inclusions confirmed in writing are the two things that matter to us, and to my parents who are contributing. Calm close, not pushy.

unanswered_questions: If we marry legally in Sydney and celebrate overseas, should the legal ceremony come before or after the celebration abroad, and does the order cause any problems?
Who is actually on the ground on the day overseas: our Wedded Advisor, or local suppliers we've never met?
What's the difference between Wedded Concierge and a Wedded Advisor? Is the Concierge a service and the Advisor the person?
Can the symbolic ceremony abroad reuse most of this script (minus the legal lines), or does it need to be written differently?
Is there a real wedding we can see where a couple married legally at home and celebrated abroad?

turn_offs_found.quote: Celebrant: "These rings hold everything you have just said to each other."
turn_offs_found.why: A bit sentimental. It's the one line in the script that could make us look try-hard in front of our friends.

turn_offs_found.quote: If this ceremony is one moment in a longer weekend, with guests flying in and a venue to secure, Wedded Concierge plans the whole celebration around it.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Plans the whole celebration' is the vague end-to-end promise we're sceptical of, and it interrupts the script. Not a hard sell, but it feels slotted in.

would_share_with: James (partner), so we can agree on vow order and the short legal option
Our celebrant, once we've chosen one, as the working draft
Whoever does the reading, so they can see where it sits

cta_reaction.quote: When the ceremony is set, your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: We'd click to see what the Concierge page says, and the AUD quotes and written inclusions are reassuring. But we're about 14 months out with no destination chosen, and we usually read two or three posts and look at a real wedding before we enquire. This post earns a bookmark, not an enquiry yet.

top_3_changes: Spell out what Wedded Concierge does in the mid-script call to action, using the same venue, travel and vendors wording the overseas section already uses, so it doesn't read as a vague 'end-to-end' promise.
Swap the sentimental ring-exchange celebrant line for a plain, neutral cue so the sample script stays understated.
Split the long opening sentence and say what the monitum is before naming the section, so a skimming partner gets it on the first pass.

suggested_edits.where: A short legal script, final paragraph (primary CTA)
suggested_edits.old: If this ceremony is one moment in a longer weekend, with guests flying in and a venue to secure, [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=wedding-ceremony-script-australia&utm_content=primary) plans the whole celebration around it.
suggested_edits.new: If this ceremony is one moment in a longer weekend, with guests flying in and a venue to secure, a Wedded Advisor from [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=wedding-ceremony-script-australia&utm_content=primary) can plan the venue, travel and vendors around it as your single point of contact.
suggested_edits.why: Replaces the vague 'plans the whole celebration' with wording the draft already uses in the overseas section (venue, travel, vendors, single point of contact). No new facts.

suggested_edits.old: Celebrant: "These rings hold everything you have just said to each other."
suggested_edits.new: Celebrant: "[Name] and [Name] will now exchange rings."
suggested_edits.why: A neutral cue reads as understated. Couples can add sentiment themselves, so the sample doesn't push a line that might feel try-hard.

suggested_edits.old: In Australia, a celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination must say the monitum in section 46(1) of the Marriage Act 1961, which opens "I am duly authorised by law to solemnise marriages according to law", or words to that effect, before you are married.
suggested_edits.new: In Australia, a celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination must say a short statement called the monitum before you are married. It is set out in section 46(1) of the Marriage Act 1961 and opens "I am duly authorised by law to solemnise marriages according to law", or words to that effect.
suggested_edits.why: Same facts, split into two sentences, and explains 'monitum' before it is cited. The 'short statement' wording is already in the draft's monitum section. Keep the existing fact_18 comment after the new second sentence.

Unknowns (who is on the ground, Concierge vs Advisor, real weddings) are in unanswered_questions, not asserted.

checks.note: Edits reuse wording already in the draft.

Did not invent problems; positives recorded where the draft earned them

open_questions.question: Several of our questions (legal ceremony before or after the overseas celebration; who is on the ground abroad) are only answerable from sources or brand facts. Should the editor add sourced sequencing guidance or a link to an existing guide, or leave this to the linked legal-vs-symbolic article?
Can a real-wedding link (legal at home, celebration abroad) be added if one exists in the link map? For this persona, real weddings are the trigger to enquire.

assumptions: Arrived from a Google search for the primary keyword while in early research, about 14 months out, no destination chosen.
The repeated 'General information... not legal advice' line is a compliance requirement, so it is noted as low-severity boredom without a suggested edit.
